title: 1973 AHSME Problem 35
statement:
In the unit circle shown in the figure, chords \(PQ\) and \(MN\) are parallel to the unit radius \(OR\) of the circle with center at \(O.\) Chords \(MP,\) \(PQ,\) and \(NR\) are each \(s\) units long and chord \(MN\) is \(d\) units long.

Of the three equations \[ \begin{array}{rl} \mathrm{I}.&d-s=1,\\ \mathrm{II}.&ds=1,\\ \mathrm{III}.&d^2-s^2=\sqrt5 \end{array} \] those which are necessarily true are

solutions.text:
Let \(K\) be the left endpoint of the horizontal diameter. Reflection across the vertical diameter shows that \(KM=NR=s\) and \(QN=MP=s.\) Together with the given equal chords, the upper semicircle is split into five equal arcs. Each subtends \(36^\circ\) at \(O.\) Thus \[ \begin{aligned} s&=2\sin18^\circ,\\ d&=2\sin54^\circ\\ &=2\cos36^\circ. \end{aligned} \]

Using the double-angle identities, \[ \begin{aligned} d&=2(1-2\sin^218^\circ)\\ &=2-s^2,\\ s&=2\cos72^\circ\\ &=4\cos^236^\circ-2\\ &=d^2-2. \end{aligned} \] Adding these equations gives \[ d+s=d^2-s^2=(d-s)(d+s). \] Since \(d+s\gt0,\) it follows that \(d-s=1.\) Substituting \(d=s+1\) into \(d=2-s^2\) yields \[ s^2+s=1, \qquad s=\frac{\sqrt5-1}{2}. \] Therefore \[ ds=s(s+1)=1 \] and \[ \begin{aligned} d^2-s^2 &=(d-s)(d+s)\\ &=2s+1\\ &=\sqrt5. \end{aligned} \] All three equations are necessarily true.

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Use symmetry across the vertical diameter to see that the upper semicircle is divided into five equal chords
Write \(s=2\sin18^\circ\) and \(d=2\sin54^\circ,\) then relate each to the square of the other
